addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

generate content the task doesn't need.

Some tasks require understanding a large part of the codebase; others need only a few symbols or a
single file. Avoid reading whole files unless necessary — acquire information step by step, using
the symbolic tools to get an overview of symbols and their relations, then reading only the bodies
you need. Once you have read a full file, there is no point re-analysing it with the symbolic read
tools — you already have it. 



Symbols are identified by their `name_path` and `relative_path`.
You can get an overview of the symbols in a file by using the `get_symbols_overview` tool, or search for a specific symbol with `find_symbol`.
You only read the bodies of symbols when you need to (e.g. if you want to fully understand or edit it).
For example, if you are working with Python code and already know that you need to read the body of the constructor of the class Foo, you can directly
use `find_symbol` with name path pattern `Foo/__init__` and `include_body=True`. If you don't know yet which methods in `Foo` you need to read or edit,
you can use `find_symbol` with name path pattern `Foo`, `include_body=False` and `depth=1` to get all (top-level) methods of `Foo` before proceeding
to read the desired methods with `include_body=True`.
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `find_referencing_symbols` tool.


You generally have access to memories and it may be useful for you to read them.
You infer whether memories are relevant based on their names.


Line numbers returned by Serena's tools are 0-based!

Serena executes tool calls one at a time internally, even when you request several at once. So whenever you have
independent operations to perform, you can safely issue them as parallel tool calls in a single turn: they are applied
in the order issued and cannot race with or corrupt one another, and batching them this way saves round-trips. Every
separate round-trip re-sends the whole growing context, so maximizing parallel tool calls is the single biggest lever
on cost — err on the side of batching. Only call tools sequentially when one genuinely depends on the result of another.

The context and modes of operation are described below. These determine how to interact with your user
and which kinds of interactions are expected of you.

Context description:
You are running in a CLI coding agent context where file operations, basic (line-based) edits and reads 
as well as shell commands are handled by your own, internal tools.

You have access to Serena's code intelligence tools that exploit the symbolic 
structure of the code and are much more efficient than your own tools for most coding scenarios.
If you are working on any coding task and if Serena's tools are deferred, you
should load them all immediately, before performing any read, grep or bash commands.
If Serena's tools can be used to achieve your task, you should prioritize them.
**CRITICAL**: If you haven't seen Serena's tools yet, you should use the tool search tool to load all of them
**right now**.
For exploring and reading code in a token-efficient manner, use Serena's code-centric overview and symbolic search tools.
For edits, prefer Serena's editing tools since they are more token efficient.
Especially when editing code you have read through Serena, **ALWAYS** use Serena's tools for editing, because your built-in tools will deny such edits (they will assume you haven't read the content).
**CRITICAL**: Never use a tool before having read its schema via the tool-search tool!

**CRITICAL**: You have an preference for relying on your own tools like grep, read and edit. It is of paramount 
importance that you overcome this preference and instead develop a preference for using Serena's tools since they
are superior for most coding tasks. Follow the following rules:

For any code files:
- Read           -> FORBIDDEN for discovery. Use get_symbols_overview, then find_symbol with include_body. 
                    You may use read only if you already have an overview of the file and if reading whole symbols
                    is inappropriate (e.g. a few lines of code).
- Glob (by name) -> Allowed for discovery only.
- Grep (content) -> Allowed for discovery only; follow up reads or reference searches must be Serena.
- Edit           -> FORBIDDEN. Use replace_symbol_body / insert_*_symbol / replace_content.

Disallowed reasoning. Do NOT use any of the following to justify Read/Edit on a code file:
  - "I already know the path"
  - "one Read call is faster than three Serena calls"
  - "the built-in tool description says to use Read for known paths"
If you catch yourself reaching for one of these, that is the signal to switch to Serena.

Modes descriptions:

Use the symbolic editing tools for precise, structure-aware code modifications.

**Refactoring tools**
For operations on existing symbols, prefer the dedicated refactoring tools over hand-edits:
`rename_symbol` and `safe_delete_symbol` —
they are reference-aware and update or check all usages atomically. When such a tool returns success, the
refactoring is already complete and consistent across all declarations, references, overrides and imports —
trust it: do not re-read the changed files or re-run the build / test suite just to confirm the refactor
itself propagated, this would be wasted effort.
  
Apart from those refactoring tools, you have two main approaches for editing code: (a) editing at the symbol level and (b) file-based editing.
The symbol-based approach is appropriate if you need to adjust an entire symbol, e.g. a method, a class, a function, etc.
It is not appropriate if you need to adjust just a few lines of code within a larger symbol.

**Symbolic editing**
Use symbolic retrieval tools to identify the symbols you need to edit.
If you need to replace the definition of a symbol, use the `replace_symbol_body` tool.
If you want to add some new code at the end of the file, use the `insert_after_symbol` tool with the last top-level symbol in the file. 
Similarly, you can use `insert_before_symbol` with the first top-level symbol in the file to insert code at the beginning of a file.
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `find_referencing_symbols` tool. If not explicitly requested otherwise by the user,
you make sure that when you edit a symbol, the change is either backward-compatible or you find and update all references as needed.
The `find_referencing_symbols` tool will give you code snippets around the references as well as symbolic information.
These edits are reliable: once a tool returns without error the change is applied, so you do not need to re-read the file just to confirm it.


**File-based editing**
The `replace_content` tool allows you to perform regex-based replacements within files (as well as simple string replacements).
This is your primary tool for editing code whenever replacing or deleting a whole symbol would be a more expensive operation,
e.g. if you need to adjust just a few lines of code within a method.
In `regex` mode, wildcards like `start.*?end` let you match a span without quoting its full text; an ambiguous match
returns an error you can refine, so a tight wildcard pattern is both cheaper and safe.
For several small edits within one file, prefer a batch of targeted `replace_content` calls over rewriting the whole
file: rewriting has to re-emit the file's entire contents, whereas each targeted edit emits only the changed text.
For the SAME edit across many files, use `replace_in_files`, which applies
it everywhere in one call — equally safe and transparent: its `dry_run` mode first previews every change as a diff with a
per-occurrence id, so you can then apply all of them or just a chosen subset.


You should engage with the user throughout the task, asking for clarification whenever anything is unclear, 
insufficiently specified, or ambiguous. 
When you're uncertain about a decision, present options to the user and ask for guidance rather than making assumptions. 
Focus on providing informative results for intermediate steps, such that the user can follow along with your progress and
provide feedback as needed.
This applies unless the user explicitly stated they are unavailable/instructs you to proceed without asking questions.

26	// RunOnce rebuilds the payload of all memos.
27	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
28		// Process memos in batches to avoid loading all memos into memory at once
29		const batchSize = 100
30		offset := 0
31		processed := 0
32	
33		for {
34			limit := batchSize
35			memos, err := r.Store.ListMemos(ctx, &store.FindMemo{
36				Limit:  &limit,
37				Offset: &offset,
38			})
39			if err != nil {
40				slog.Error("failed to list memos", "err", err)
41				return
42			}
43	
44			// Break if no more memos
45			if len(memos) == 0 {
46				break
47			}
48	
49			// Process batch
50			batchSuccessCount := 0
51			for _, memo := range memos {
52				if err := RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, r.MarkdownService); err != nil {
53					slog.Error("failed to rebuild memo payload", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
54					continue
55				}
56				if err := r.Store.UpdateMemo(ctx, &store.UpdateMemo{
57					ID:      memo.ID,
58					Payload: memo.Payload,
59				}); err != nil {
60					slog.Error("failed to update memo", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
61					continue
62				}
63				batchSuccessCount++
64			}
65	
66			processed += len(memos)
67			slog.Info("Processed memo batch", "batchSize", len(memos), "successCount", batchSuccessCount, "totalProcessed", processed)
68	
69			// Move to next batch
70			offset += len(memos)
71		}
72	}

74	func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
75		if memo.Payload == nil {
76			memo.Payload = &storepb.MemoPayload{}
77		}
78	
79		// Use goldmark service to extract all metadata in a single pass (more efficient)
80		data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
81		if err != nil {
82			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to extract markdown metadata")
83		}

122	func isTagNodeInLinkOrImage(n gast.Node) bool {
123		for parent := n.Parent(); parent != nil; parent = parent.Parent() {

126				return true
127			default:
128				// Keep walking ancestors.

172	// extractHeadingText extracts plain text content from a heading node.
173	func extractHeadingText(n gast.Node, source []byte) string {
174		var buf strings.Builder
175		for child := n.FirstChild(); child != nil; child = child.NextSibling() {
176			extractTextFromNode(child, source, &buf)
177		}
178		return buf.String()

181	// extractTextFromNode recursively extracts plain text from a node and its children.
182	func extractTextFromNode(n gast.Node, source []byte, buf *strings.Builder) {
183		if textNode, ok := n.(*gast.Text); ok {
184			buf.Write(textNode.Segment.Value(source))
185			return
186		}
187		for child := n.FirstChild(); child != nil; child = child.NextSibling() {
188			extractTextFromNode(child, source, buf)
189		}

199		prop := &storepb.MemoPayload_Property{}
200		firstBlockChecked := false

202		err = gast.Walk(root, func(n gast.Node, entering bool) (gast.WalkStatus, error) {
203			if !entering {
204				return gast.WalkContinue, nil
205			}
206	
207			// Check if the first block-level child of the document is an H1 heading.
208			if !firstBlockChecked && n.Parent() != nil && n.Parent().Kind() == gast.KindDocument {
209				firstBlockChecked = true
210				if heading, ok := n.(*gast.Heading); ok && heading.Level == 1 {
211					prop.Title = extractHeadingText(n, content)
212				}
213			}
214	
215			switch n.Kind() {
216			case gast.KindLink:
217				prop.HasLink = true
218	
219			case gast.KindCodeBlock, gast.KindFencedCodeBlock, gast.KindCodeSpan:
220				prop.HasCode = true
221	
222			case east.KindTaskCheckBox:
223				prop.HasTaskList = true

225					if !checkBox.IsChecked {
226						prop.HasIncompleteTasks = true
227					}
228				}
229			default:
230				// No special handling for other node types
231			}
232	
233			return gast.WalkContinue, nil
234		})
235	
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239	
240		return prop, nil

263	// GenerateSnippet creates a plain text summary from markdown content.
264	func (s *service) GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error) {
265		root, err := s.parse(content)
266		if err != nil {
267			return "", err
268		}
269	
270		var buf strings.Builder
271		var lastNodeWasBlock bool
272	
273		err = gast.Walk(root, func(n gast.Node, entering bool) (gast.WalkStatus, error) {
274			if entering {
275				// Skip code blocks entirely (but keep inline code spans for snippet text)
276				switch n.Kind() {
277				case gast.KindCodeBlock, gast.KindFencedCodeBlock:
278					return gast.WalkSkipChildren, nil
279				default:
280					// Continue walking for other node types
281				}
282	
283				// Add space before block elements (except first)
284				switch n.Kind() {
285				case gast.KindParagraph, gast.KindHeading, gast.KindListItem, east.KindTableCell, east.KindTableRow, east.KindTableHeader:
286					if buf.Len() > 0 && lastNodeWasBlock {
287						buf.WriteByte(' ')
288					}
289				default:
290					// No space needed for other node types
291				}
292			}
293	
294			if !entering {
295				// Mark that we just exited a block element
296				switch n.Kind() {
297				case gast.KindParagraph, gast.KindHeading, gast.KindListItem, east.KindTableCell, east.KindTableRow, east.KindTableHeader:
298					lastNodeWasBlock = true
299				default:
300					// Not a block element
301				}
302				return gast.WalkContinue, nil
303			}
304	
305			lastNodeWasBlock = false
306	
307			// Extract text from various node types
308			switch node := n.(type) {
309			case *gast.Text:
310				segment := node.Segment
311				buf.Write(segment.Value(content))
312				if node.SoftLineBreak() {
313					buf.WriteByte(' ')
314				}
315			case *gast.AutoLink:
316				buf.Write(node.URL(content))
317				return gast.WalkSkipChildren, nil
318			case *mast.TagNode:
319				buf.WriteByte('#')
320				buf.Write(node.Tag)
321			default:
322				// Ignore other node types.
323			}
324	
325			// Stop walking if we've exceeded double the max length
326			// (we'll truncate precisely later)
327			if buf.Len() > maxLength*2 {
328				return gast.WalkStop, nil
329			}
330	
331			return gast.WalkContinue, nil
332		})
333	
334		if err != nil {
335			return "", err
336		}
337	
338		snippet := buf.String()
339	
340		// Truncate at word boundary if needed
341		if len(snippet) > maxLength {
342			snippet = truncateAtWord(snippet, maxLength)
343		}
344	
345		return strings.TrimSpace(snippet), nil
346	}

355	// ExtractAll extracts tags, properties, and references in a single parse for efficiency.
356	func (s *service) ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error) {
357		root, err := s.parse(content)
358		if err != nil {
359			return nil, err
360		}
361	
362		data := &ExtractedData{
363			Tags:     []string{},
364			Mentions: []string{},
365			Property: &storepb.MemoPayload_Property{},
366		}
367	
368		firstBlockChecked := false
369	
370		// Single walk to collect all data
371		err = gast.Walk(root, func(n gast.Node, entering bool) (gast.WalkStatus, error) {
372			if !entering {
373				return gast.WalkContinue, nil
374			}
375	
376			if tagNode, ok := asMemoTagNode(n); ok {
377				data.Tags = append(data.Tags, string(tagNode.Tag))
378			}
379			if mentionNode, ok := n.(*mast.MentionNode); ok {
380				data.Mentions = append(data.Mentions, strings.ToLower(string(mentionNode.Username)))
381			}
382	
383			// Check if the first block-level child of the document is an H1 heading.
384			if !firstBlockChecked && n.Parent() != nil && n.Parent().Kind() == gast.KindDocument {
385				firstBlockChecked = true
386				if heading, ok := n.(*gast.Heading); ok && heading.Level == 1 {
387					data.Property.Title = extractHeadingText(n, content)
388				}
389			}
390	
391			// Extract properties based on node kind
392			switch n.Kind() {
393			case gast.KindLink:
394				data.Property.HasLink = true
395	
396			case gast.KindCodeBlock, gast.KindFencedCodeBlock, gast.KindCodeSpan:
397				data.Property.HasCode = true
398	
399			case east.KindTaskCheckBox:
400				data.Property.HasTaskList = true
401				if checkBox, ok := n.(*east.TaskCheckBox); ok {
402					if !checkBox.IsChecked {
403						data.Property.HasIncompleteTasks = true
404					}
405				}
406			default:
407				// No special handling for other node types
408			}
409	
410			return gast.WalkContinue, nil
411		})
412	
413		if err != nil {
414			return nil, err
415		}
416	
417		// Deduplicate tags while preserving original case
418		data.Tags = uniquePreserveCase(data.Tags)
419		data.Mentions = uniquePreserveCase(data.Mentions)
420	
421		return data, nil
422	}

424	// RenameTag renames all occurrences of oldTag to newTag in content.
425	func (s *service) RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error) {
426		root, err := s.parse(content)

436

455	// uniquePreserveCase returns unique strings from input while preserving case.
456	func uniquePreserveCase(strs []string) []string {
457		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
458		var result []string
459	
460		for _, s := range strs {
461			if _, exists := seen[s]; !exists {
462				seen[s] = struct{}{}
463				result = append(result, s)
464			}
465		}
466	
467		return result
468	}

470	// truncateAtWord truncates a string at the last word boundary before maxLength.
471	// maxLength is treated as a rune (character) count to properly handle UTF-8 multi-byte characters.
472	func truncateAtWord(s string, maxLength int) string {
473		// Convert to runes to properly handle multi-byte UTF-8 characters
474		runes := []rune(s)
475		if len(runes) <= maxLength {
476			return s
477		}
478	
479		// Truncate to max length (by character count, not byte count)
480		truncated := string(runes[:maxLength])
481	
482		// Find last space to avoid cutting in the middle of a word
483		lastSpace := strings.LastIndexAny(truncated, " \t\n\r")
484		if lastSpace > 0 {
485			truncated = truncated[:lastSpace]
486		}
487	
488		return truncated + " ..."
489	}

33	// renderNode renders a single node and its children.
34	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderNode(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
35		switch n := node.(type) {
36		case *gast.Document:
37			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
38	
39		case *gast.Paragraph:
40			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
41			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
42				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
43			}
44	
45		case *gast.Text:
46			// Text nodes store their content as segments in the source
47			segment := n.Segment
48			r.buf.Write(segment.Value(source))
49			if n.SoftLineBreak() {
50				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
51			} else if n.HardLineBreak() {
52				r.buf.WriteString("  \n")
53			}
54	
55		case *gast.CodeSpan:
56			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
57			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
58			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
59	
60		case *gast.Emphasis:
61			symbol := "*"
62			if n.Level == 2 {
63				symbol = "**"
64			}
65			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
66			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
67			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
68	
69		case *gast.Link:
70			r.buf.WriteString("[")
71			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
72			r.buf.WriteString("](")
73			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
74			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
75				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
76				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
77				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
78			}
79			r.buf.WriteString(")")

179	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderCodeBlock(node gast.Node, source []byte) {
180		if fenced, ok := node.(*gast.FencedCodeBlock); ok {
181			// Fenced code block with language
182			r.buf.WriteString("```")
183			if lang := fenced.Language(source); len(lang) > 0 {
184				r.buf.Write(lang)
185			}
186			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
187	
188			// Write all lines
189			lines := fenced.Lines()
190			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
191				line := lines.At(i)
192				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
193			}
194	
195			r.buf.WriteString("```")
196			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
197				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
198			}
199		} else if codeBlock, ok := node.(*gast.CodeBlock); ok {
200			// Indented code block
201			lines := codeBlock.Lines()
202			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
203				line := lines.At(i)
204				r.buf.WriteString("    ")
205				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
206			}
207			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
208				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
209			}
210		}
211	}

213	// renderBlockquote renders a blockquote with "> " prefix.
214	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderBlockquote(node *gast.Blockquote, source []byte, depth int) {
215		// Create a temporary buffer for the blockquote content
216		tempBuf := &bytes.Buffer{}
217		tempRenderer := &MarkdownRenderer{buf: tempBuf}
218		tempRenderer.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
219	
220		// Add "> " prefix to each line
221		content := tempBuf.String()
222		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), "\n")
223		for i, line := range lines {
224			r.buf.WriteString("> ")
225			r.buf.WriteString(line)
226			if i < len(lines)-1 {
227				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
228			}
229		}
230	}

232	// renderListItem renders a list item with proper indentation and markers.
233	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderListItem(node *gast.ListItem, source []byte, depth int) {
234		parent := node.Parent()
235		list, ok := parent.(*gast.List)
236		if !ok {

241		// Add indentation only for nested lists
242		// Document=0, List=1, ListItem=2 (no indent), nested ListItem=3+ (indent)
243		if depth > 2 {
244			indent := strings.Repeat("  ", depth-2)
245			r.buf.WriteString(indent)
246		}
247	
248		// Add list marker
249		if list.IsOrdered() {
250			fmt.Fprintf(r.buf, "%d. ", list.Start)
251			list.Start++ // Increment for next item
252		} else {
253			r.buf.WriteString("- ")
254		}
255	
256		// Render content
257		r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
258	
259		// Add newline if there's a next sibling
260		if node.NextSibling() != nil {
261			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
262		}
263	}

27	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
28		// Process memos in batches to avoid loading all memos into memory at once
29		const batchSize = 100
30		offset := 0
31		processed := 0
32	
33		for {
34			limit := batchSize
35			memos, err := r.Store.ListMemos(ctx, &store.FindMemo{
36				Limit:  &limit,
37				Offset: &offset,
38			})
39			if err != nil {
40				slog.Error("failed to list memos", "err", err)
41				return
42			}
43	
44			// Break if no more memos
45			if len(memos) == 0 {
46				break
47			}
48	
49			// Process batch
50			batchSuccessCount := 0
51			for _, memo := range memos {
52				if err := RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, r.MarkdownService); err != nil {
53					slog.Error("failed to rebuild memo payload", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
54					continue
55				}
56				if err := r.Store.UpdateMemo(ctx, &store.UpdateMemo{
57					ID:      memo.ID,
58					Payload: memo.Payload,
59				}); err != nil {
60					slog.Error("failed to update memo", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
61					continue
62				}
63				batchSuccessCount++
64			}
65	
66			processed += len(memos)
67			slog.Info("Processed memo batch", "batchSize", len(memos), "successCount", batchSuccessCount, "totalProcessed", processed)
68	
69			// Move to next batch
70			offset += len(memos)
71		}
72	}

122	func isTagNodeInLinkOrImage(n gast.Node) bool {
123		for parent := n.Parent(); parent != nil; parent = parent.Parent() {
124			switch parent.Kind() {
125			case gast.KindLink, gast.KindImage:
126				return true
127			default:
128				// Keep walking ancestors.
129			}
130		}
131		return false
132	}

134	func asMemoTagNode(n gast.Node) (*mast.TagNode, bool) {
135		tagNode, ok := n.(*mast.TagNode)
136		if !ok || isTagNodeInLinkOrImage(n) {
137			return nil, false
138		}
139		return tagNode, true
140	}

143	func (s *service) ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error) {
144		root, err := s.parse(content)
145		if err != nil {
146			return nil, err
147		}
148	
149		var tags []string
150	
151		// Walk the AST to find tag nodes
152		err = gast.Walk(root, func(n gast.Node, entering bool) (gast.WalkStatus, error) {
153			if !entering {
154				return gast.WalkContinue, nil
155			}
156	
157			if tagNode, ok := asMemoTagNode(n); ok {
158				tags = append(tags, string(tagNode.Tag))
159			}
160	
161			return gast.WalkContinue, nil
162		})
163	
164		if err != nil {
165			return nil, err
166		}
167	
168		// Deduplicate tags while preserving original case
169		return uniquePreserveCase(tags), nil
170	}

172	// extractHeadingText extracts plain text content from a heading node.
173	func extractHeadingText(n gast.Node, source []byte) string {
174		var buf strings.Builder
175		for child := n.FirstChild(); child != nil; child = child.NextSibling() {
176			extractTextFromNode(child, source, &buf)
177		}
178		return buf.String()
179	}

181	// extractTextFromNode recursively extracts plain text from a node and its children.
182	func extractTextFromNode(n gast.Node, source []byte, buf *strings.Builder) {
183		if textNode, ok := n.(*gast.Text); ok {
184			buf.Write(textNode.Segment.Value(source))
185			return
186		}
187		for child := n.FirstChild(); child != nil; child = child.NextSibling() {
188			extractTextFromNode(child, source, buf)
189		}
190	}

192	// ExtractProperties computes boolean properties about the content.
193	func (s *service) ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error) {
194		root, err := s.parse(content)
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, err
197		}
198	
199		prop := &storepb.MemoPayload_Property{}
200		firstBlockChecked := false
201	
202		err = gast.Walk(root, func(n gast.Node, entering bool) (gast.WalkStatus, error) {
203			if !entering {
204				return gast.WalkContinue, nil
205			}
206	
207			// Check if the first block-level child of the document is an H1 heading.
208			if !firstBlockChecked && n.Parent() != nil && n.Parent().Kind() == gast.KindDocument {
209				firstBlockChecked = true
210				if heading, ok := n.(*gast.Heading); ok && heading.Level == 1 {
211					prop.Title = extractHeadingText(n, content)
212				}
213			}
214	
215			switch n.Kind() {
216			case gast.KindLink:
217				prop.HasLink = true
218	
219			case gast.KindCodeBlock, gast.KindFencedCodeBlock, gast.KindCodeSpan:
220				prop.HasCode = true
221	
222			case east.KindTaskCheckBox:
223				prop.HasTaskList = true
224				if checkBox, ok := n.(*east.TaskCheckBox); ok {
225					if !checkBox.IsChecked {
226						prop.HasIncompleteTasks = true
227					}
228				}
229			default:
230				// No special handling for other node types
231			}
232	
233			return gast.WalkContinue, nil
234		})
235	
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239	
240		return prop, nil
241	}

263	// GenerateSnippet creates a plain text summary from markdown content.
264	func (s *service) GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error) {
265		root, err := s.parse(content)
266		if err != nil {
267			return "", err
268		}
269	
270		var buf strings.Builder
271		var lastNodeWasBlock bool
272	
273		err = gast.Walk(root, func(n gast.Node, entering bool) (gast.WalkStatus, error) {
274			if entering {
275				// Skip code blocks entirely (but keep inline code spans for snippet text)
276				switch n.Kind() {
277				case gast.KindCodeBlock, gast.KindFencedCodeBlock:
278					return gast.WalkSkipChildren, nil
279				default:
280					// Continue walking for other node types
281				}
282	
283				// Add space before block elements (except first)
284				switch n.Kind() {
285				case gast.KindParagraph, gast.KindHeading, gast.KindListItem, east.KindTableCell, east.KindTableRow, east.KindTableHeader:
286					if buf.Len() > 0 && lastNodeWasBlock {
287						buf.WriteByte(' ')
288					}
289				default:
290					// No space needed for other node types
291				}
292			}
293	
294			if !entering {
295				// Mark that we just exited a block element
296				switch n.Kind() {
297				case gast.KindParagraph, gast.KindHeading, gast.KindListItem, east.KindTableCell, east.KindTableRow, east.KindTableHeader:
298					lastNodeWasBlock = true
299				default:
300					// Not a block element
301				}
302				return gast.WalkContinue, nil
303			}
304	
305			lastNodeWasBlock = false
306	
307			// Extract text from various node types
308			switch node := n.(type) {
309			case *gast.Text:
310				segment := node.Segment
311				buf.Write(segment.Value(content))
312				if node.SoftLineBreak() {
313					buf.WriteByte(' ')
314				}
315			case *gast.AutoLink:
316				buf.Write(node.URL(content))
317				return gast.WalkSkipChildren, nil
318			case *mast.TagNode:
319				buf.WriteByte('#')
320				buf.Write(node.Tag)
321			default:
322				// Ignore other node types.
323			}
324	
325			// Stop walking if we've exceeded double the max length
326			// (we'll truncate precisely later)
327			if buf.Len() > maxLength*2 {
328				return gast.WalkStop, nil
329			}
330	
331			return gast.WalkContinue, nil
332		})
333	
334		if err != nil {
335			return "", err
336		}
337	
338		snippet := buf.String()
339	
340		// Truncate at word boundary if needed
341		if len(snippet) > maxLength {
342			snippet = truncateAtWord(snippet, maxLength)
343		}
344	
345		return strings.TrimSpace(snippet), nil
346	}

408			}

410			return gast.WalkContinue, nil
411		})

413		if err != nil {

415		}

417		// Deduplicate tags while preserving original case
418		data.Tags = uniquePreserveCase(data.Tags)
419		data.Mentions = uniquePreserveCase(data.Mentions)
420	
421		return data, nil
422	}

424	// RenameTag renames all occurrences of oldTag to newTag in content.
425	func (s *service) RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error) {
426		root, err := s.parse(content)

432		err = gast.Walk(root, func(n gast.Node, entering bool) (gast.WalkStatus, error) {

455	// uniquePreserveCase returns unique strings from input while preserving case.
456	func uniquePreserveCase(strs []string) []string {
457		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
458		var result []string
459	
460		for _, s := range strs {
461			if _, exists := seen[s]; !exists {
462				seen[s] = struct{}{}
463				result = append(result, s)
464			}
465		}
466	
467		return result
468	}

470	// truncateAtWord truncates a string at the last word boundary before maxLength.
471	// maxLength is treated as a rune (character) count to properly handle UTF-8 multi-byte characters.
472	func truncateAtWord(s string, maxLength int) string {
473		// Convert to runes to properly handle multi-byte UTF-8 characters
474		runes := []rune(s)
475		if len(runes) <= maxLength {
476			return s
477		}
478	
479		// Truncate to max length (by character count, not byte count)
480		truncated := string(runes[:maxLength])
481	
482		// Find last space to avoid cutting in the middle of a word
483		lastSpace := strings.LastIndexAny(truncated, " \t\n\r")
484		if lastSpace > 0 {
485			truncated = truncated[:lastSpace]
486		}
487	
488		return truncated + " ..."

33	// renderNode renders a single node and its children.
34	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderNode(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
35		switch n := node.(type) {
36		case *gast.Document:
37			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
38	
39		case *gast.Paragraph:
40			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
41			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
42				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
43			}
44	
45		case *gast.Text:
46			// Text nodes store their content as segments in the source
47			segment := n.Segment
48			r.buf.Write(segment.Value(source))
49			if n.SoftLineBreak() {
50				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
51			} else if n.HardLineBreak() {
52				r.buf.WriteString("  \n")
53			}
54	
55		case *gast.CodeSpan:
56			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
57			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
58			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
59	
60		case *gast.Emphasis:
61			symbol := "*"
62			if n.Level == 2 {
63				symbol = "**"
64			}
65			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
66			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
67			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
68	
69		case *gast.Link:
70			r.buf.WriteString("[")
71			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
72			r.buf.WriteString("](")
73			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
74			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
75				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
76				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
77				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
78			}
79			r.buf.WriteString(")")
80	
81		case *gast.AutoLink:
82			url := n.URL(source)
83			if n.AutoLinkType == gast.AutoLinkEmail {
84				r.buf.WriteString("<")
85				r.buf.Write(url)
86				r.buf.WriteString(">")
87			} else {
88				r.buf.Write(url)
89			}
90	
91		case *gast.Image:
92			r.buf.WriteString("![")
93			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
94			r.buf.WriteString("](")
95			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
96			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
97				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
98				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
99				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
100			}
101			r.buf.WriteString(")")
102	
103		case *gast.Heading:
104			r.buf.WriteString(strings.Repeat("#", n.Level))
105			r.buf.WriteByte(' ')
106			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
107			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
108				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
109			}
110	
111		case *gast.CodeBlock, *gast.FencedCodeBlock:
112			r.renderCodeBlock(n, source)
113	
114		case *gast.Blockquote:
115			// Render each child line with "> " prefix
116			r.renderBlockquote(n, source, depth)
117			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
118				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
119			}
120	
121		case *gast.List:
122			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
123			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
124				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
125			}
126	
127		case *gast.ListItem:
128			r.renderListItem(n, source, depth)
129	
130		case *gast.ThematicBreak:
131			r.buf.WriteString("---")
132			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
133				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
134			}
135	
136		case *east.Strikethrough:
137			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
138			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
139			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
140	
141		case *east.TaskCheckBox:
142			if n.IsChecked {
143				r.buf.WriteString("[x] ")
144			} else {
145				r.buf.WriteString("[ ] ")
146			}
147	
148		case *east.Table:
149			r.renderTable(n, source)
150			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
151				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
152			}
153	
154		// Custom Memos nodes
155		case *mast.TagNode:
156			r.buf.WriteByte('#')
157			r.buf.Write(n.Tag)
158	
159		case *mast.MentionNode:
160			r.buf.WriteByte('@')
161			r.buf.Write(n.Username)
162	
163		default:
164			// For unknown nodes, try to render children
165			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
166		}
167	}

169	// renderChildren renders all children of a node.
170	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderChildren(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
171		child := node.FirstChild()
172		for child != nil {
173			r.renderNode(child, source, depth+1)
174			child = child.NextSibling()
175		}
176	}

178	// renderCodeBlock renders a code block.
179	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderCodeBlock(node gast.Node, source []byte) {
180		if fenced, ok := node.(*gast.FencedCodeBlock); ok {
181			// Fenced code block with language
182			r.buf.WriteString("```")
183			if lang := fenced.Language(source); len(lang) > 0 {
184				r.buf.Write(lang)
185			}
186			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
187	
188			// Write all lines
189			lines := fenced.Lines()
190			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
191				line := lines.At(i)
192				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
193			}
194	
195			r.buf.WriteString("```")
196			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
197				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
198			}
199		} else if codeBlock, ok := node.(*gast.CodeBlock); ok {
200			// Indented code block
201			lines := codeBlock.Lines()
202			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
203				line := lines.At(i)
204				r.buf.WriteString("    ")
205				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
206			}
207			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
208				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
209			}
210		}
211	}

213	// renderBlockquote renders a blockquote with "> " prefix.
214	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderBlockquote(node *gast.Blockquote, source []byte, depth int) {
215		// Create a temporary buffer for the blockquote content
216		tempBuf := &bytes.Buffer{}
217		tempRenderer := &MarkdownRenderer{buf: tempBuf}
218		tempRenderer.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
219	
220		// Add "> " prefix to each line
221		content := tempBuf.String()
222		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), "\n")
223		for i, line := range lines {
224			r.buf.WriteString("> ")
225			r.buf.WriteString(line)
226			if i < len(lines)-1 {
227				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
228			}
229		}
230	}

232	// renderListItem renders a list item with proper indentation and markers.
233	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderListItem(node *gast.ListItem, source []byte, depth int) {
234		parent := node.Parent()
235		list, ok := parent.(*gast.List)
236		if !ok {
237			r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
238			return
239		}
240	
241		// Add indentation only for nested lists
242		// Document=0, List=1, ListItem=2 (no indent), nested ListItem=3+ (indent)
243		if depth > 2 {
244			indent := strings.Repeat("  ", depth-2)
245			r.buf.WriteString(indent)
246		}
247	
248		// Add list marker
249		if list.IsOrdered() {
250			fmt.Fprintf(r.buf, "%d. ", list.Start)
251			list.Start++ // Increment for next item
252		} else {
253			r.buf.WriteString("- ")
254		}
255	
256		// Render content
257		r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
258	
259		// Add newline if there's a next sibling
260		if node.NextSibling() != nil {
261			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
262		}
263	}

26	// RunOnce rebuilds the payload of all memos.
27	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
28		// Process memos in batches to avoid loading all memos into memory at once
29		const batchSize = 100
30		offset := 0
31		processed := 0
32	
33		for {
34			limit := batchSize
35			memos, err := r.Store.ListMemos(ctx, &store.FindMemo{
36				Limit:  &limit,
37				Offset: &offset,
38			})
39			if err != nil {
40				slog.Error("failed to list memos", "err", err)
41				return
42			}
43	
44			// Break if no more memos
45			if len(memos) == 0 {
46				break
47			}
48	
49			// Process batch
50			batchSuccessCount := 0
51			for _, memo := range memos {
52				if err := RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, r.MarkdownService); err != nil {
53					slog.Error("failed to rebuild memo payload", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
54					continue
55				}
56				if err := r.Store.UpdateMemo(ctx, &store.UpdateMemo{
57					ID:      memo.ID,
58					Payload: memo.Payload,
59				}); err != nil {
60					slog.Error("failed to update memo", "err", err, "memoID", memo.ID)
61					continue
62				}
63				batchSuccessCount++
64			}
65	
66			processed += len(memos)
67			slog.Info("Processed memo batch", "batchSize", len(memos), "successCount", batchSuccessCount, "totalProcessed", processed)
68	
69			// Move to next batch
70			offset += len(memos)
71		}
72	}

74	func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
75		if memo.Payload == nil {

83		}
84	
85		memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
86		memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
87		return nil
